dedupe_keys.name: lahore and rawalpindi methane and leachate from municipal solid waste dumpsites estimated with landgem

description: This case study estimates greenhouse gas emissions and leachate from the main municipal solid waste disposal sites of Lahore and Rawalpindi, two of the largest cities in Punjab, Pakistan. The authors published it as an open-access journal article. Emissions were estimated and projected over a 50-year active timespan with the US EPA LandGEM model following the 2006 IPCC guidelines, using waste disposal quantities for each site, and leachate generation was estimated alongside. Coverage is the dumpsites serving the two cities. The article is free under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Caveats: waste quantities and composition in Pakistan are poorly recorded, LandGEM default parameters add uncertainty, and the sites are largely unmanaged dumpsites for which the model was not designed. The study estimated cumulative emissions from Lahore's disposal sites at about 133,446 gigagrams, equal to 108 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (26 percent methane, 73 percent carbon dioxide), against 958 gigagrams or 7.8 million tonnes for Rawalpindi, and called for methane capture, leachate treatment and waste-to-energy. Simulation uses: an example for climate adaptation and mitigation planning and investment appraisal in the waste sector, and for groundwater risk screening near dumpsites. Related records: the LandGEM model (model-landgem), and the Lahore IoT waste collection pilot (case_study-lahore-iot-waste-collection-pilot) on the collection side.
